translations.meta.description: ui5-pdfme user guide for designing, checking, saving, and printing PDF templates.
translations.meta.title: ui5-pdfme · User guide
translations.hero.p.1: Learn to open a template, insert content, check the result, and save the design without needing to understand its technical integration.
translations.hero.figcaption.1: Audio: English · Captions off
translations.hero.p.2: Play the video in English · Reproducir el vídeo en español
translations.purpose.p.1: ui5-pdfme combines a visual design with fields supplied by the application. The result is a reusable template that can generate many documents with different data.
translations.purpose.p.2: Add text, tables, images, signatures, shapes, dates, and codes; position them and adjust their properties.
translations.purpose.p.3: Insert fields from the data panel so the application fills the document automatically.
translations.purpose.p.4: Check the PDF, save the template, and download or print the final document.
translations.purpose.div.1: Important: a template stores the design, not credentials or permissions. The application decides which data and repositories each person may use.
translations.screen.p.1: Select a numbered area in the image to discover what you can do there.
translations.screen.attr-alt.1: Editor with six interactive areas: templates, top toolbar, data fields, palette, canvas, and field list
translations.screen.figcaption.1: Select an area directly on the screenshot or use the area buttons. The layout becomes compact on narrow screens, but the operations remain the same.
translations.screen.p.2: Open the catalog to search, filter, and retrieve saved designs.
translations.screen.p.3: Use it when: you want to start from an existing template instead of the current design.
translations.screen.p.4: Save the template, preview, download, or print the PDF, and access help or full screen.
translations.screen.p.5: Tip: preview before downloading or printing to inspect the actual output.
translations.screen.p.6: Shows available values. Selecting a field inserts it into the document and connects it to application data.
translations.screen.p.7: Tip: use search and check whether the field is included or not included.
translations.screen.p.8: Adds static content such as text, images, tables, shapes, or dates. Barcodes and QR groups the available code formats.
translations.screen.p.9: Use it when: the content does not need to get its value from data.
translations.screen.p.10: Represents the document pages. Select, move, and resize each element here.
translations.screen.p.11: Tip: select an element to see its settings and drag it to change its position.
translations.screen.p.12: Locates an element and changes its identifier, content, style, and behavior.
translations.screen.p.13: Tip: use a short, semantic, unique identifier for every field.
translations.screen.attr-alt.2: Crop of the top toolbar with the Templates and PDF preview buttons
translations.screen.figcaption.2:
Open and check

Templates opens the catalog. The same toolbar contains PDF preview, download, print, help, and full screen.
translations.screen.attr-alt.3: Crop of the Data fields panel and the side palette
translations.screen.figcaption.3:
Add content

Data fields are on the left. Immediately to their right, the side palette creates static content.
translations.screen.attr-alt.4: Crop of the central canvas and the Field List on the right
translations.screen.figcaption.4:
Edit the design

The canvas occupies the center. The Field List and properties are on the right to locate and configure each element.
translations.first-document.li.1: Open a template. Select Templates, use filters if needed, and choose Open. If there is no catalog, work with the design prepared by the application.
translations.first-document.li.2: Add content. Select a field from the left panel to connect it to data, or choose a type from the palette to create static content.
translations.first-document.li.3: Position it. Drag the element on the canvas and use its handles to resize it.
translations.first-document.li.4: Configure it. Select the element and review its properties. Use a short, semantic, unique identifier.
translations.first-document.li.5: Check the result. Select PDF preview. Correct the design until its data is easy to read.
translations.first-document.li.6: Save. Enter a name, description, tags, status, and repository the first time.
translations.fields.td.2: Titles, labels, instructions, lines, and decorative elements.
translations.fields.td.3: Keeps the content written in the template and shows an eye in the list. When repeated on every page, it also shows the stacked-pages icon. Value from data remains off.
translations.fields.td.5: Customer, date, amount, address, items, and any changing value.
translations.fields.td.6: Receives a value from the application. It shows the database icon and Value from data is on.
translations.fields.p.1: This is the stable key connecting the design to its data. It must be unique across the whole template. Do not use translated text shown to the recipient; names such as customerName, invoiceDate, or items are preferable.
translations.fields.h3.2: Label and value in one Text field
translations.fields.p.2: For a connected Text, enable Show label and edit Label text to render a compact field such as Subtotal: $125.50. The label is visible in the layout and is included in preview and the final PDF. For static Text, the flag remains checked and disabled because the template content already is its visible text.
translations.fields.li.1: Use search to locate a field by its path or sample value.
translations.fields.li.2: Included means the design already uses that value; it does not necessarily mean it is visible on the current page.
translations.fields.li.3: Not included means no element uses that value yet.
translations.fields.li.4: Select refresh when the application has changed its sample data.
translations.advanced.p.1: Insert the field representing the complete collection, not just a property from its first row. Adjust headers, widths, and height with empty, small, and large examples.
translations.advanced.p.2: Use it for sentences combining fixed text with several values, such as a summary with invoice number, customer, and total. Keep every variable available in the data.
translations.advanced.p.3: Reserve enough space and check their quality in the generated PDF. Under Barcodes and QR, choose QR, Code 128, EAN-13, Data Matrix, or PDF417. Verify each code with a real scanner before publishing the template.
translations.advanced.p.4: For a static header or footer, or a data-bound Text field, enable Fixed non-moving position. The element keeps its coordinates and stays outside the flow when tables or text grow. You may then enable Repeat on every page; the Text's resolved value is repeated too. Otherwise it is drawn only on its original page. During generation, the repeated element's boundary automatically extends the nearest top or bottom page padding so content that moves to another page cannot overlap it; configured padding remains the minimum. Repeated static text may use {currentPage} and {totalPages}. These options are hidden for connected fields other than Text and when the background is an imported PDF.
translations.templates.p.1: The first time, Save template requests metadata. Later saves update the open record unless the application provides a specific operation for creating another version.
translations.templates.td.2: Describe the document and, when relevant, its country or language.
translations.templates.td.4: State the purpose, recipient, and relevant special behavior.
translations.templates.td.6: Use consistent terms that make searching easier.
translations.templates.td.8: A design in progress or awaiting review.
translations.templates.td.10: A version approved for operational use.
translations.templates.td.12: A design kept for historical purposes but not recommended for new documents.
translations.templates.div.1: Changing status is not an approval by itself. Available permissions, reviews, and versions depend on the system hosting the editor.
translations.templates.p.2: To configure where designs are listed and saved, see the technical Template catalog and repositories guide.
translations.validate.li.1: Refresh the data and open PDF preview.
translations.validate.li.2: Check empty values, very long text, and special characters.
translations.validate.li.3: Test tables with no rows, one row, and many rows.
translations.validate.li.4: Review page breaks, margins, and content outside the printable area.
translations.validate.li.5: Verify language, dates, timezone, currency, and fonts.
translations.validate.li.6: Download a PDF and open it outside the editor.
translations.validate.li.7: Make a test print when physical size matters.
translations.validate.p.1: Browsers show their own print dialog. The editor cannot print silently.
translations.troubleshooting.td.2: Select refresh. If the panel remains empty, the application has not supplied data or you lack access; contact the functional owner.
translations.troubleshooting.td.3: A field is empty in the PDF
translations.troubleshooting.td.4: Check that it is connected, its identifier matches an available option, and the sample data has a value.
translations.troubleshooting.td.6: Choose an available option for a connected field or use a unique name for a static field.
translations.troubleshooting.td.8: Select a static element or a connected Text. These options are unavailable for other connected fields and imported PDF backgrounds.
translations.troubleshooting.td.10: Increase its space, reduce columns or text, and test with more rows. Review the following page too.
translations.troubleshooting.td.12: Check the selected repository and status. The application may limit these operations according to your permissions.
translations.troubleshooting.td.13: The print dialog does not appear
translations.troubleshooting.td.14: Allow the PDF to finish generating and check whether the browser blocked the dialog or new window.
translations.glossary.td.1: The reusable design of a document.
translations.glossary.td.2: An element placed on a page.
translations.glossary.td.3: An element whose value comes from application data.
translations.glossary.td.4: The stable, unique name connecting a field to its value.
translations.glossary.td.5: The source used to find and save templates.
translations.glossary.td.6: A generated PDF used to check the result before downloading or printing.
